speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We adopt this approach because the measure involved is market-sensitive and needs to be effected shortly after the Bill has been announced.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In order to read the Bill three times in single Parliamentary Sitting, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) has sought and obtained the President's certification that the urgency exists for this Bill under Standing Order 86 of the Standing Orders of the Parliament of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: PHEs are defined as entities whose primary tangible assets are residential properties in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, the acquisition of shares in companies is subject to 0.2% stamp duty, based on the purchase price of the value of the shares.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is no stamp duty on the acquisition of equity interest for other types of entities, such as partnerships and trusts, or the disposal of equity interests in all types of entities, including companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This treatment applies even when the entity's assets mainly comprise residential properties in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In comparison, the purchase of residential properties in Singapore attracts Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) of 1% to 3% and Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) of up to 15%.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Both BSD and ABSD are based on the purchase price or the value of the properties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The sale of residential properties in Singapore may also be subject to Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is, therefore, a stamp duty rate differential between the buying or selling of residential properties and the buying or selling of equity interest in entities holding residential properties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With ABSD and SSD remaining relevant in our property market, we have decided that it is timely to close this stamp duty rate differential.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is just like how we currently levy BSD or ABSD, and ABSD or SSD, on the purchase or sale of residential property, even if the purchase or sale is for bona fide business reasons.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The new ACD will apply, in addition to the prevailing stamp duty of 0.2%, for the transfer of shares in companies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should highlight that the measure will not impact the ordinary buying and selling of shares by retail investors in entities listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, they are not subject to share duties where the shares are scripless and no document is executed for the transfer of such shares.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Rather, ACD is aimed at the transfer of equity interest in PHEs by significant owners of such entities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Specifically, an entity is regarded as a PHE under two circumstances.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The first category of entities holds residential properties directly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To establish if such an entity is a PHE, we will apply a significant asset test.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will call this a Type One PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is also a second category of entities that have indirect holdings of residential property through Type One entities in which they have at least 50% equity interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The entity may also own some residential properties directly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For such an entity, it will be considered a PHE if it meets two criteria.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, it beneficially owns at least 50% equity interest in a Type One PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, it meets the significant asset test as mentioned above.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, the total value of the residential property it hence owns indirectly through these Type One PHEs, as well as the value of the residential property it may own directly, comprises 50% or more of its total tangible assets.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: ACD will apply to acquisition or disposal of equity interest by owners with significant equity interest in the PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To be considered a significant owner, one has to either presently hold at least 50% equity interest in a PHE or hold at least 50% interest after the equity acquisition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In determining whether the 50% ownership threshold for significant ownership is met, we will take into account the equity interest held by associates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Examples of associates include a parent company and its subsidiary or, in the context of individuals, a father and his children, husband and wife.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also cover arrangements under which individual buyers act in concert to purchase shares with the objective of avoiding the new duties.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This serves to mitigate any potential attempt to circumvent the 50% ownership threshold through its associates and thus avoid ACD for purchase or sale of its equity interest in a PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The computation of ACD will be based on the prevailing market value of the underlying residential property at the time of the qualifying acquisition or disposal of equity interest, in proportion to equity interest.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This flat 15% rate applies irrespective of whether the buyer of the equity interest is a Singaporean, a Permanent Resident, a foreigner or a non-individual entity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, a disposal of equity interest will be subject to ACD for the seller if: (a) the disposal is made after the seller has become a significant owner; (b) the equity interest disposed of is acquired on or after 11 March 2017; (c) the equity interest disposed of is held for three years or less from the time of acquisition.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This flat rate applies, irrespective of the holding period for the equity interest which is disposed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I should also clarify that once a person acquires equity interest on or after 11 March 2017 in a PHE and becomes a significant owner of such a PHE, ACD on sale of equity interest will continue to apply and to such time that the owner has disposed completely of all the equity interest in the PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To deter potential attempt by the buyer and seller to circumvent the provisions for the new duties, the Bill includes a specific anti-avoidance provision.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This provision charges the new duties notwithstanding the conditions are not met, for instance, if an arrangement was made with the purpose of allowing an entity to be no longer a PHE.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The duty is not chargeable if the Commissioner is of the opinion that the arrangement was not carried out to avoid the duty.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The remaining legislative changes are mostly technical in nature.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On that, Mdm Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am pleasantly surprised by the speed that my suggestion has been taken up.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I do not think the Ministry could have come up with the Bill within such a short time, so I am sure the Ministry had been looking at this issue for some time.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Quoting recent newspaper articles after Minister Lawrence Wong talked about this during his Committee of Supply (COS) speech, this move is seen by some industry players as plugging an existing regulatory loophole.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would like MOF to consider if a separate taskforce can be set up specifically to look at whether there are other loopholes across the various Ministries which we have to plug.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This taskforce should also look at other creative ways to increase Government revenues.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope the Ministry will be able to find more revenue sources which are both progressive, in that only the rich pays, and discretionary, in that they have a choice.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The increase in Additional Registration Fee for luxury cars in early 2013 is one such example of a tax which is both progressive and discretionary.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In terms of finding new sources of revenue, for instance, we may consider whether it makes sense to tender out car registration number plates with alphabet series which are no longer available.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For example, I think a two-letter SG series number plate will be very well received.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As a responsible and prudent Government, we have always tried to run a balanced Budget.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But it will become increasingly challenging as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I hope that with additional revenue sources which are both progressive and discretionary, we will not need to increase other taxes which may impact low- to middle-income families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is something that we have been monitoring quite carefully and we have been studying this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Members can appreciate, the design of the scheme itself and the issues at stake are quite complex.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not a revenue-raising measure per se but the motivation for doing this is to remove the existing differential in the stamp duty rates, which I have explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With regard to revenue issues, we have already spoken about this at length during the Budget Debate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Minister for Finance has highlighted our approach for new sources of revenue in his round-up speech and we had a discussion on this in the COS for MOF as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are studying all options carefully to determine the best way to raise revenues to support our future expenditure needs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I just have one question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Does this new Bill provide some flexibility to address, should, in the future, the property players come up with more ingenious or some creative way to counter this?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Are there provisions for that without having to come to Parliament to do another amendment?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will have to continue to study this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: After putting in this measure, I think there will be adjustment in the way industry players respond to this, so we will have to monitor very carefully.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have also put in place flexibility provisions so that even after this measure, we can make further changes if need be.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: One, whether the Minister feels this stabilises the property market, especially the high-end market which has been quite sluggish.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Two, the real problem really seems to be an oversupply of private properties, whether the Ministry will also address this.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Third, while we pass this Bill with such haste, will this not actually just result in a huge transaction in the next few hours?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If this was done in haste, we would have probably done it much earlier.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the impact of the property market and the broader issues of high-end residential property market, whether there is, indeed, an oversupply, that is a separate matter regarding property market conditions in general.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not want to get too much into that debate but it would suffice to say that our aim is to ensure a stable and sustainable property market in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is what we seek to do and we are continuously monitoring the property market conditions to achieve this objective.

speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
text: I support the Bill because it levels the playing field for payment of stamp duties.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we do not have data on the numbers who are doing it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We believe it is the right thing to do and we had taken time and effort to study this to make sure that whatever measures we are putting in place are balanced, appropriate and do not also impact negatively on legitimate business transactions.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Also, I know the tax is on the underlying residential property value.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the case of a distress sale, in a hurry, how would you determine the value of the asset?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The criteria and the test that we have laid out are very clearly spelt out, so we will use this objectively.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On valuation, there are clearly spelt out valuation methods to do valuations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not think we need to get into a debate on that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think these valuation methodologies are already in place today to value properties.
